original_question: (D. Segal). A group word w is said to be concise in a class C of groups if for every group G in C such that the set Gw of word values of w in G is finite, the verbal subgroup w(G) = ⟨Gw ⟩ is also finite(see also Archive 2.45). Is every word concise in the class of residually finite groups? See(D. Segal, Words. Notes on verbal width in groups, Cambridge Univ. Press, 2009) for a partial solution.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.105 in "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": the Segal problem asking whether every group word is concise in the class of residually finite groups, with an explicit cross-reference to Archive 2.45. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it correctly names D. Segal, states the definition of conciseness using finiteness of G_w and the verbal subgroup w(G)=⟨G_w⟩, asks exactly about the class of residually finite groups, mentions the cross-reference to Archive 2.45, and retains the paper's note that Segal's 2009 book contains a partial solution. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the universal quantification should be explicit: the problem is about every group word w and every residually finite group G. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The notation is best standardized as G_w for the set of all values of w in G; the paper uses this notation in Problem 21.105. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The generic class C belongs only to the definition of conciseness; in the actual question one specializes C to the class of residually finite groups. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Archive 2.45 is a historical pointer to Hall's original conciseness problem, not an extra hypothesis or a separate part of the formal question. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The sentence referring to Segal's 2009 book records partial progress but is not itself part of the mathematical statement to be asked. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let w be a group word. For a residually finite group G, let G_w denote the set of all values of w in G, and let w(G)=⟨G_w⟩ be the corresponding verbal subgroup. If G_w is finite, must w(G) also be finite? Equivalently, is every group word concise in the class of residually finite groups?
justification: Problem 21.105 states essentially your draft verbatim. The only real refinements needed are presentational: make the quantifiers explicit, standardize the notation G_w, and isolate the actual yes/no problem from the surrounding historical note about Archive 2.45 and the bibliographic note about Segal's partial solution. The cross-reference to Archive 2.45 shows that 21.105 is the residually finite analogue of Hall's original conciseness question, while the immediately following Problem 21.106 is a different question about first-order formulas, so the scope should remain exactly at group words. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
